replies.hint: Reverse everything after the first character, then place the first character at the end.
replies.concept: Strings of length 0 or 1 are already reversed.
replies.complexity: Conceptually O(n) recursive calls; repeated slicing/concatenation can make the Python implementation O(n²) time and space.

replies.hint: Treat the last list item as the base case. Compare the current item with the maximum of the remaining items.
replies.concept: Passing an index avoids creating a new sliced list during each call.

replies.hint: At each level make two choices. When the current string reaches length n, store it and return.
replies.concept: This is a recursion tree with two branches at every level and is the foundation of backtracking.
replies.complexity: There are 2ⁿ outputs, each of length n: time O(n·2ⁿ), output/working space O(n·2ⁿ).
